title: SIG questionnaire walkthrough - Arcadia Insurance
next_steps: Send completed SIG spreadsheet with column-level notes
Share redacted SOC 2 Type II report and control mappings
Schedule a technical deep dive for KMS/HSM integration with Arcadia security team week of 2026-02-09
Provide audit log retention samples and configuration docs
action_items: Maya Patel - Upload redacted SOC 2 Type II and point to control mappings in shared drive by 2026-02-12
Ethan Ross - Prepare brief on KMS/HSM options (AWS KMS vs customer-managed HSM) and sample configuration by 2026-02-10
Lena Ortiz - Send Arcadia's vendor risk form sections for data residency mapping by 2026-02-08
summary: Walkthrough of Arcadia's SIG questionnaire. Discussed SOC 2 evidence, SSO/SAML and RBAC, encryption/KMS options, audit log retention, and data residency requirements. Agreed next steps to share SOC 2 Type II, KMS deep dive, and complete SIG spreadsheet.
topics: SOC 2 Type II and evidence requests
Encryption at rest and KMS/HSM options
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Lena Ortiz: Hi, Lena here, Security Manager at Arcadia.
[00:09] Tom Blake: Tom Blake, IT Ops.
[00:11] Sophie Lee: Sophie, procurement.
[00:13] Ethan Ross: Ethan Ross from Redwood, I'm the SE, I'll walk through the technical bits.
[00:17] Maya Patel: Great. The main goal today is the SIG/CAIQ walkthrough you sent over, go through answers and evidence ask and identify any blockers. We'll keep this recorded.
[00:27] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. We mostly want to know what evidence you can provide for the usual items SOC 2, encryption, RBAC, audit logs, data residency.
[00:35] Ethan Ross: Perfect. I'll start with a high level then we'll go line-by-line on the spreadsheet. Note in advance some of our docs are redacted but we can provide attestations and screenshots.
[00:44] Maya Patel: Quick timeline question - you're targeting vendor approval by end of Feb, Sophie?
[00:49] Sophie Lee: Yes procurement hopes to have contract in place early March, so late Feb approval would be ideal.
[00:54] Maya Patel: Good, that aligns. Ok Ethan, go ahead.
[00:58] Ethan Ross: K, first section SOC 2 - we are SOC 2 Type II in 2025, I think the latest report is available, we will share a redacted copy. For control mappings we can provide the complementing SOC control matrix that maps to SIG sections.
[01:12] Lena Ortiz: When you say redacted, what gets redacted? Keys, customer names?
[01:16] Ethan Ross: Typically we redact customer names and internal IP addresses and some network diagrams that show customer specifics; we keep control descriptions, exception periods, and auditor opinion intact.
[01:25] Tom Blake: Do you have any compensating controls for multi-tenant isolation? We need assurance around noisy neighbor and KV cache leaks.
[01:33] Ethan Ross: Yeah, good question. Our runtime uses tenant isolation at the process and GPU allocation level; we can provide architecture diag, though some of the infra-level details might be obfuscated. We also have prefix/KV cache separation per customer and rate-limited access. I'll add a note in the spreadsheet cell.
[01:48] Maya Patel: I'll flag that we should include a screenshot of your tenant isolation dashboard and a short paragraph on KV cache separation.
[01:54] Lena Ortiz: Ok. Next SSO and RBAC. We use Okta and we need SAML 2.0, SCIM provisioning, and role-based separation.
[02:03] Ethan Ross: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM-based provisioning for user sync. Roles can be mapped to RBAC groups; we also support role scoping per project. We can share a runbook, example SAML metadata, and a SCIM sample payload.
[02:19] Sophie Lee: Does SCIM support custom attributes? We need an attribute for cost-center for entitlements.
[02:24] Ethan Ross: There's a custom attribute mapping for SCIM yes, we can map cost_center to group assignment rules. Will confirm exact attribute name.
[02:30] Lena Ortiz: Is there MFA enforced?
[02:33] Ethan Ross: MFA is enforced via the customer's IdP policy; Redwood supports enforcement flags but the IdP controls the MFA requirement.
[02:41] Maya Patel: Next up encryption. Arcadia asked about encryption at rest and KMS options.
[02:47] Ethan Ross: By default data at rest is encrypted using provider-managed keys (AES-256). For customer-managed keys we support AWS KMS CMEK and also can integrate with external HSMs for private deployments. In Hosted mode we offer KMS integration with CMKs; Dedicated/Private can use customer HSMs.
[03:04] Tom Blake: We need to use our own KMS and have key rotation controls. Can you support bringing our CMK and rotate keys on schedule?
[03:12] Ethan Ross: Yes, we support customer-managed CMKs and key rotation schedules. For some private deployments we can also integrate with FIPS 140-2 HSMs — for on-prem we can accommodate HSMs behind the VPC. I'll prepare a short doc on the integration steps.
[03:26] Lena Ortiz: Do you have envelope encryption?
[03:29] Ethan Ross: Yes envelope encryption is used — data keys encrypted by the CMK, and we rotate data keys periodically. We'll include a diagram.
[03:36] Maya Patel: Good. Audit logs and retention?
[03:39] Ethan Ross: We retain audit logs for 90 days by default in hosted plan; Dedicated/Enterprise can configure retention up to 7 years and we can push logs to customer-owned S3/GCS for long-term retention. Logs include API calls, model selection, token usage, and admin actions.
[03:56] Sophie Lee: Are logs tamper-evident / append-only? We need chain of custody for forensics.
[04:01] Ethan Ross: We support write-once storage options and immutability via object-lock on customer buckets if they export logs. In-hosted we provide signed hashes of log batches to detect tamper.
[04:12] Lena Ortiz: Can we get a sample log and schema?
[04:15] Ethan Ross: Yes I'll upload a sanitized sample log and the JSON schema.
[04:19] Maya Patel: Data residency — Arcadia requires EU-only processing for EU customers and no replication outside EU.
[04:26] Tom Blake: Correct, and we need contractual guarantees plus proof of region isolation.
[04:29] Ethan Ross: We support regional pinning; hosted model routing can be constrained to EU regions. For Dedicated and Private we can ensure physical location. We'll provide the dataflow diagrams and the contract clause language we use for data residency.
[04:42] Lena Ortiz: What about backups? Are backups replicated globally?
[04:45] Ethan Ross: By default backups reside in the same region; we can opt out of cross-region replication for EU-only customers. We'll include backup policy notes.
[04:54] Maya Patel: A couple of SIG-specific questions: CAIQ section on network segmentation, vulnerability management, and incident response.
[04:59] Ethan Ross: For vuln mgmt we run monthly internal scans and quarterly external pen tests, with triage SLAs. Incident response has a playbook and we provide timeline notifications within our SLA; dedicated customers can have custom escalation chains.
[05:14] Lena Ortiz: Can you provide pen test summary and evidence of remediation?
[05:18] Ethan Ross: We can provide summary reports and remediation attestations; raw penetration test reports are redacted but we can provide evidence of ticketing and timelines.
[05:26] Sophie Lee: On legal we need indemnities and data processing addendum. Maya, is that in the standard contract?
[05:31] Maya Patel: Yes DSPA and DPA clauses are standard for enterprise deals; we'll surface the DPA language in the contract.
[05:36] Tom Blake: A few nitty-gritty items in the SIG spreadsheet — some cells ask for encryption algorithm names and key lengths.
[05:43] Ethan Ross: We use AES-256-GCM for data at rest, TLS 1.2+ with strong ciphers in transit. KDF and HMAC details I'll add to the spreadsheet.
[05:52] Lena Ortiz: On monitoring and alerting — will you send security alerts to our PagerDuty?
[05:56] Ethan Ross: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we can integrate with your PagerDuty, Slack, or email. For hosted we have webhooks and alert subscriptions.
[06:05] Maya Patel: Ok, time check — we're at about 36 minutes in, let's call out open items and owners.
[06:12] Ethan Ross: Open items: share redacted SOC 2 and control mapping (Maya/Ethan), upload sample audit logs and schema (Ethan), prepare KMS/HSM options doc and integration steps (Ethan), confirm SCIM custom attribute mapping (Ethan), confirm backup replication settings for EU-only (Maya) — anything to add?
[06:31] Lena Ortiz: Please also add the pen test summary and remediation evidence.
[06:34] Ethan Ross: Will do.
[06:36] Sophie Lee: Procurement asks for estimated cost delta for dedicated vs hosted for a 24/7 low-latency SLA — rough numbers?
[06:44] Maya Patel: We can send a pricing sheet — there's typically a 2-3x uplift for Dedicated depending on GPU tiers. I'll include a ballpark and recommend a follow-up with capacity profile.
[06:55] Tom Blake: For the evidence submission process, what format do you prefer? PDF uploads, secure portal?
[07:01] Ethan Ross: We use a secure vendor portal for evidence uploads — SAML-protected and with audit trails. We'll invite Arcadia and provide instructions.
[07:10] Lena Ortiz: Great. Any risks or blockers we should call out?
[07:13] Ethan Ross: The main potential blocker is if Arcadia requires full unredacted infra diagrams or raw pen test reports; those are typically restricted. We can offer attestations and remediation records but not expose customer details or vendor internal secrets.
[07:28] Maya Patel: Ok let's recap next steps.
[07:31] Maya Patel: We'll send the redacted SOC 2 and control mapping, Ethan will upload sample logs and KMS integration doc, we will complete the SIG spreadsheet cells with notes and evidence links, and schedule a technical deep dive for KMS the week of Feb 9.
[07:46] Sophie Lee: That works.
[07:48] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all.
[07:50] Ethan Ross: Thanks, we'll share items by the due dates.
[07:53] Maya Patel: End meeting.
questions: Can Redwood provide redacted SOC 2 Type II and control mapping?
Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS and HSMs?
Can audit logs be exported to customer-owned storage with immutability?
